domain_label: Knowledge-Graph Relation Validation — LLM Claim Verification with Calibrated Confidence & Abstention (evidence-grounded entailment/contradiction judgment of each (A,relation,B) proposition, ECE-aware confidence, mandatory abstention below threshold, relation-type/negation correction, and verifying the human flag itself)
purpose: The content-level truth layer of the kgverify specialist: how a relation-validation authority judges whether each (A, relation, B) proposition is clinically/anatomically TRUE, using evidence-grounded NLI-style entailment/contradiction verification rather than model memory, with CALIBRATED confidence (ECE-aware), MANDATORY abstention below threshold, and guards against LLM overconfidence — producing a typed truth verdict (true / false / mistyped / inverted / negation / UNKNOWN) plus a confidence for each candidate defect the deterministic layer (kb1) hands it. It verifies the graph AND the human flag (the D2 'non-sequitur' that is actually a real association), it can correct a relation TYPE or propose a negation, and it never asserts a clinical fact without a citation or an explicit UNKNOWN. It defers structure to kgraph, render to viz, scheduling to learner/sched, and the repair proposal/provenance to kb3.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all base metric scores are heuristic priors and every design call is an ESTIMATE synthesized from the cited literature and app grounding files

external method claims are grounded in published work and carried inline as [FACT-source: URL]; publisher pages returned 403 to direct fetch (bot-block, not a proxy failure), so citations rest on search-engine summaries that quote those papers and any figure not directly quoted is left unstated rather than invented

clinical claims about the D2 malignancy associations (marantic/nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis; PTHrP paraneoplastic hypercalcemia) are tagged CLINICAL-UNKNOWN with a high prior and must be verified against a citation before assertion — consistent with kgverify's own doctrine
raw LLM confidence is treated as an ESTIMATE, never a FACT, and is only trusted after calibration is checked; the specific verifier model and its ECE are session UNKNOWNs to confirm by recon

this KB is the CONTENT-LEVEL TRUTH (LLM verification) third of the kgverify specialist; deterministic logical/mereological detection and owner-gated repair/provenance are neighboring KBs this one consumes candidates from and hands verdicts to
exclusions: the deterministic logical/mereological detection that produces the candidate defects (kb1) beyond consuming its typed candidate list
the repair proposal, owner-gating, and immutable provenance record of any correction (kb3) beyond emitting a typed truth verdict a proposal is built from

all graph SCHEMA/STRUCTURE governance — whether the corrected/retyped/negated edge is a legal edge, per-type directionality, DAG acyclicity, closed-vocabulary changes, node granularity, hub detection (owned by kgraph)
the render of a verdict, a correction status, or a negated edge (owned by viz) and the mastery-estimation and spaced-repetition scheduling math (owned by learner/sched)

building the retrieval index, the verifier model, or the pipeline in the app (owned by app engineering/extint) beyond specifying the evidence-grounded, calibrated, abstaining verification method such code must implement

competency_questions.question: What does the content-level truth layer own, and how is it distinct from deterministic detection (kb1) and from graph structure (kgraph)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states this KB judges whether each (A,relation,B) proposition is clinically true, consumes kb1's candidate defects, and defers structure to kgraph and repair/provenance to kb3

competency_questions.question: How is each proposition verified — as what kind of judgment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: casts verification as an NLI-style entailment/contradiction judgment combining contradiction testing and conservative filtering

competency_questions.question: Why must verification be evidence-grounded rather than grounded in model memory?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: prefers retrieval-augmented verification that avoids internal LLM factual knowledge and compares statements to retrieved external document chunks, so a verdict traces to evidence

competency_questions.question: Why can the specialist trust neither the graph nor the human flag, and what does D2 illustrate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states both the graph and the owner's flag can be wrong, that malignancy→marantic endocarditis and malignancy→PTHrP are plausibly real (CLINICAL-UNKNOWN, verify), and that the likely defect is a wrong relation TYPE not a false proposition

competency_questions.question: How is confidence made trustworthy, and why is raw model confidence not a FACT?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: measures fact-checking by Expected Calibration Error, notes verbal confidence depends on calibration and prompt design, and treats raw confidence as ESTIMATE

competency_questions.question: How is LLM overconfidence guarded against?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: notes LLMs show Dunning-Kruger-like overconfidence in fact-checking so raw confidence is never promoted to FACT and overconfidence is actively guarded

competency_questions.question: Why is abstention a first-class output and how is it scored?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states a desirable model answers when confident and abstains when uncertain, scored by selective accuracy, abstention-friendly accuracy and certainty rate, and returns UNKNOWN/no-proposal below threshold

competency_questions.question: How does confidence gate the expensive verification path?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: uses prediction confidence as a signal to selectively trigger deep retrieval/calibration rather than applying it to all instances, so high-agreement edges pass cheaply

competency_questions.question: What multi-signal scoring raises reliability beyond a single judgment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: uses an LLM-as-judge per-triple reliability score, schema-aware verification as strategic planning/investigation/evidential reasoning, and self-agreement across samples as a calibration proxy

competency_questions.question: How does the verifier correct a relation TYPE rather than only judging true/false?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: can output 'proposition plausibly true but relation TYPE wrong' (retype related→causal, or fix direction) and hands the schema legality of the new type to kgraph

competency_questions.question: How can a negation be a verdict, and what is the rule about rendering it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: can conclude 'A does NOT relate to B' and propose a negated edge, never emitting a bare deletion where the truth is a negation and never rendering a negation positive (render owned by viz)

competency_questions.question: How is a verdict labeled for honesty, and when does the specialist abstain to UNKNOWN?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: labels every verdict FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN, requires a verdict to trace to evidence or be an explicit UNKNOWN, and quarantines unverifiable propositions

competency_questions.question: What happens when model calibration is untrusted or drifts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: on overconfidence signals, prompt-sensitivity or ECE degradation, lowers autonomy by widening the human-review band and treating all confidences as ESTIMATE

competency_questions.question: How are thin nodes (D3) re-linked without fabrication, and how does the verdict map onto the app?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: proposes candidate edges for thin nodes only with a citation (no gap-filling by fabrication) and maps the verdict onto ConceptEdge with an honesty tag while deferring estimation to learner/sched

competency_questions.question: What does the content-truth layer commit to as its verdict, and what does it defer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: commits to an evidence-grounded, calibrated, abstaining verifier producing a typed truth verdict plus confidence, and defers structure to kgraph, render to viz, scheduling to learner/sched, and repair/provenance to kb3

glossary.definition: Casting factuality and contradiction detection as a natural-language-inference judgment of each (A,relation,B) proposition, combining validation through contradiction testing with conservative filtering [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.19023v1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.02574].

Retrieval-augmented verification that 'avoids using internal LLM factual knowledge altogether, instead comparing verified RDF statements to chunks of external documents retrieved through web search or Wikipedia' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07507] — the honesty backbone: a verdict must trace to retrieved evidence, not model memory.

The core reason a verification specialist is needed rather than a delete pass: the owner flagged malignancy→endocarditis and malignancy→PTHrP as non-sequiturs, but malignancy→marantic/nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis and malignancy→PTHrP (paraneoplastic hypercalcemia) are plausibly real associations [CLINICAL-UNKNOWN — high prior, must verify against a citation]; the likely defect is a wrong/underspecified relation TYPE, not a false proposition — so both the graph and the human flag can be wrong.

The metric by which fact-checking confidence quality is measured; larger models' confidence better aligns with capability, but 'verbal confidence depends heavily on model calibration, which varies across LLMs and is sensitive to prompt design' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://aman.ai/primers/ai/factuality-in-LLMs/ ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.08803] — so raw confidence is ESTIMATE, never FACT.

LLMs show Dunning–Kruger-like overconfidence in fact-checking [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-39046-w], so raw model confidence is actively distrusted and never laundered into a FACT verdict.

'A desirable model should not only answer when confident but also abstain when uncertain,' scored by selective accuracy, abstention-friendly accuracy, and certainty rate [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.02574]; below the confidence threshold kgverify returns UNKNOWN / no-proposal, inheriting kgraph's abstain-rather-than-show-a-confidently-wrong-answer doctrine.

Using 'prediction confidence as a signal to selectively trigger calibration rather than applying correction to all instances' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.16555 (Retrieve-Refine-Calibrate) ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.08803]; high-agreement edges pass cheaply while only contested ones get deep retrieval and reasoning.

Raising reliability by combining an LLM-as-judge per-triple reliability score to remove low-quality triples [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.14271], schema-aware verification reframed as 'strategic planning, dynamic investigation, and evidential reasoning' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.04190], and self-agreement across samples as a calibration proxy [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.02574].

A verdict form for D2: 'proposition plausibly true but relation TYPE wrong' — retype an untyped/wrong related into a causal/associated-with edge, or fix direction — where kgverify proposes the retyping and hands the schema legality of the new type to kgraph.

The verifier can conclude 'A does NOT relate to B' and propose a NEGATED edge; kgverify never emits a bare deletion where the truth is a negation, and the negated edge must render negative (viz owns the render contract).

When no retrievable evidence exists for a proposition either way, the verdict is UNKNOWN and the proposition is quarantined and routed to a human/domain-expert; the authored glossary / source-of-record is the arbiter, not the model's memory [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07507].

nodes.definition: Frame the layer: this KB is the CONTENT-LEVEL truth third of kgverify — it judges whether each (A, relation, B) proposition is clinically/anatomically TRUE, the class of defect a rule cannot settle (kb1's deterministic layer catches the structural ones). It CONSUMES kb1's typed candidate-defect list plus the raw edges and, for each, returns a typed truth verdict — true / false / mistyped / inverted / negation / UNKNOWN — with a calibrated confidence. Feature A names exactly this: 'an AI pass that reads each (A, relation, B) proposition, judges clinical truth' [FACT-source: NEW_FEATURES_PLAN §3A]. The payoff is that a false-but-well-formed proposition (which no rule flags) is caught; the discipline is that every verdict traces to retrieved evidence or is an explicit UNKNOWN, and the layer proposes nothing structural — it hands truth to kb3 for owner-gated repair and defers schema to kgraph [ESTIMATE — design synthesis, high confidence].

included: the judges-clinical-truth frame consuming kb1's candidates
typed truth verdict + calibrated confidence per proposition
every verdict traces to evidence or is UNKNOWN; structure deferred
excluded: deterministic structural detection (kb1)
the repair proposal and provenance (kb3)
graph schema (kgraph)

proposing a structural edit the layer does not own

nodes.definition: Cast each proposition's verification as an NLI-style entailment/contradiction judgment: does the retrieved evidence ENTAIL (A, relation, B), CONTRADICT it, or leave it NEUTRAL/underdetermined? Factuality and contradiction detection are commonly framed as NLI, and recent pipelines combine 'validation through contradiction testing and conservative filtering' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.19023v1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.02574]. Entailment supports a candidate-TRUE verdict, contradiction supports FALSE or a negation, and neutral/underdetermined pushes toward abstention. Conservative filtering means the layer errs toward not asserting: a contradiction is stronger evidence to act than a weak entailment, which is why a flagged edge is contradiction-tested before it is defended or deleted.

included: entailment / contradiction / neutral as the verdict primitives
contradiction testing plus conservative filtering
neutral pushes toward abstention
excluded: where the evidence comes from (its own node)
the confidence calibration (its own node)

pros.claim: An NLI framing gives a principled three-way verdict (entail/contradict/neutral) instead of a binary true/false guess
pros.example: letting a 'neutral' evidence state map cleanly to abstention rather than a forced verdict

cons.claim: NLI over retrieved chunks can be fooled by surface similarity, entailing a proposition the evidence only superficially matches
cons.example: a chunk mentioning malignancy and endocarditis together read as entailment without the causal link being stated

failure_modes: reading co-occurrence as entailment
forcing a binary verdict where evidence is neutral
acceptance_tests: verification is cast as an entailment/contradiction/neutral judgment with contradiction testing and conservative filtering, and neutral maps to abstention
revisit_triggers: a new verdict primitive is needed

nodes.definition: Ground verification in retrieved EVIDENCE, not model memory. Prefer retrieval-augmented verification that 'avoids using internal LLM factual knowledge altogether, instead comparing verified RDF statements to chunks of external documents retrieved through web search or Wikipedia' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07507]. This is the honesty backbone: a verdict must TRACE to a retrieved document chunk, matching kgverify's boundary that it never asserts clinical truth without a citation. For D2 this is exactly what distinguishes 'malignancy→marantic endocarditis is real' (an evidence-backed defense of a surprising edge) from a hallucinated defense of a bad edge. The retrieval source/index is a session UNKNOWN to confirm by recon; until then the authored glossary / source-of-record is the fallback arbiter.

nodes.definition: Encode the D2 lesson: BOTH the graph and the human flag can be wrong, which is the core reason a verification specialist is needed rather than a delete pass. The owner marked malignancy→endocarditis and malignancy→PTHrP as non-sequiturs, but malignancy→marantic/nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis and malignancy→PTHrP (paraneoplastic hypercalcemia) are plausibly real associations [CLINICAL-UNKNOWN — high prior, must verify against a citation before asserting]. The likely defect is a wrong/underspecified relation TYPE (an untyped related where a causes/associated-with was meant), not a false proposition. So kgverify must NOT trust the flag either: it independently verifies the flagged edge against evidence and PROTECTS true-but-surprising edges from erroneous deletion. This node is why the specialist exists.

nodes.definition: Make confidence trustworthy before using it. Fact-checking quality is measured by Expected Calibration Error (ECE); larger models' confidence better aligns with actual capability, but 'verbal confidence depends heavily on model calibration, which varies across LLMs and is sensitive to prompt design' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://aman.ai/primers/ai/factuality-in-LLMs/ ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.08803]. So every confidence the verifier emits is treated as an ESTIMATE, tracked against ECE, and only used to gate action after calibration is checked; a bare model-reported probability is never promoted to a FACT verdict. The verifier's ECE for this app is a session UNKNOWN to confirm by recon — until then confidence is used conservatively (wider abstention band).

confidence is ESTIMATE, tracked, calibration-checked before use
the verifier's ECE UNKNOWN pending recon; conservative use meanwhile
excluded: the overconfidence-specific guard (its own node)
the abstention threshold mechanics (its own node)

cons.claim: Calibration is prompt-sensitive and model-specific, so an ECE measured once can drift and mislead
cons.example: a confidence that looks well-calibrated on a benchmark but is overconfident on rare clinical associations

failure_modes: promoting a raw confidence to a FACT verdict
using a stale ECE after the model or prompt changed
acceptance_tests: confidence is measured by ECE, treated as ESTIMATE, calibration-checked before gating, and the verifier's ECE is marked UNKNOWN pending recon with conservative use meanwhile
revisit_triggers: the verifier's ECE is measured by recon

nodes.definition: Actively guard against LLM overconfidence. LLMs show Dunning–Kruger-like overconfidence in fact-checking [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-39046-w], asserting wrong answers with high stated confidence — so raw model confidence is never promoted to FACT and a high-confidence verdict is not, by itself, a reason to act. The guard means: a confident verdict still requires evidence-grounding; agreement across independent signals (self-consistency, multiple retrievals) is trusted more than a single high number; and a confidently-wrong proposal is treated as WORSE than an abstention. This is the same posture kgraph takes ('a confidently wrong definition is worse than none'), applied to relation truth.

included: Dunning-Kruger-like overconfidence in LLM fact-checking
a confident verdict still needs evidence and cross-signal agreement
a confidently-wrong proposal is worse than an abstention
excluded: the calibration-drift autonomy policy (its own node)
the multi-signal scoring detail (its own node)

cons.claim: Over-distrusting confidence can push the system to abstain too often and under-correct real defects
cons.example: abstaining on a genuinely well-evidenced correction because the model also happened to sound confident

failure_modes: acting on a high stated confidence alone
abstaining so aggressively that real defects go uncorrected

nodes.definition: Make abstention a first-class output. 'A desirable model should not only answer when confident but also abstain when uncertain,' scored by selective accuracy, abstention-friendly accuracy, and certainty rate [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.02574]. Below the confidence threshold kgverify returns UNKNOWN / no-proposal, proposes nothing, and routes the proposition to human review — inheriting kgraph's 'abstain rather than show a confidently wrong definition' doctrine. Abstention rate is MEASURED, and a confidently-wrong verdict is scored worse than an abstention. This is what keeps the layer honest on the many INBDE/USMLE propositions where the retrieved evidence is genuinely underdetermined.

nodes.definition: Use confidence to gate cost. Use 'prediction confidence as a signal to selectively trigger calibration rather than applying correction to all instances' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.16555 (Retrieve-Refine-Calibrate) ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.08803]. High-agreement edges — where kb1 raised no defect and the cheap verification pass is confidently entailed — pass cheaply; only CONTESTED edges (a kb1 candidate defect, a low-confidence pass, or a human flag) get deep retrieval plus reasoning. This keeps the expensive, retrieval-heavy path off the bulk of a 162-edge graph and spends it where truth is genuinely uncertain, which is also where overconfidence is most dangerous.

high-agreement edges pass cheaply; contested edges get deep retrieval
cost concentrated where truth is uncertain
excluded: the abstention threshold itself (its own node)

cons.claim: A miscalibrated cheap pass can wave through a false edge it was overconfident about, never reaching the deep path
cons.example: an overconfident cheap entailment on a subtly-wrong edge that the deep path would have caught

failure_modes: trusting the cheap pass on a miscalibrated model
never escalating an edge the cheap pass was wrongly confident about
acceptance_tests: confidence gates the expensive path so high-agreement edges pass cheaply and contested edges (kb1 defect, low confidence, or human flag) get deep retrieval and reasoning
revisit_triggers: the cheap pass misses caught by the deep pass

nodes.definition: Raise reliability with multiple signals rather than one judgment. An LLM-as-judge predicts a per-triple RELIABILITY score to remove low-quality triples [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.14271]; schema-aware verification reframes triple-checking as 'strategic planning, dynamic investigation, and evidential reasoning' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.04190]; and self-agreement across samples is a calibration proxy [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.02574]. Combining these — an evidence-grounded entailment verdict, a reliability score, and cross-sample consistency — gives a more robust confidence than any single number, and disagreement among the signals is itself a reason to abstain or escalate. This is the antidote to single-shot overconfidence.

included: LLM-as-judge per-triple reliability score
schema-aware verification as planning/investigation/evidential reasoning
self-agreement across samples as a calibration proxy; disagreement → abstain/escalate
excluded: the single-verdict NLI primitive (its own node)
the owner-gating of the outcome (kb3)

nodes.definition: Allow a NEGATION as a verdict (D4). nodes.definition: Label every verdict for honesty. A proposition verdict is FACT only when it traces to a cited/curated source; ESTIMATE when it is LLM-inferred but evidence-linked; UNKNOWN when unverifiable. A verdict with no retrieved evidence is an abstention (UNKNOWN), not a guess; a raw LLM confidence is ESTIMATE, never FACT. This inherits kgraph's evidence-label policy verbatim and is the discipline that survives into kb3: a machine-corrected edge stays ESTIMATE until a human confirms it FACT. The label is attached at the verdict, so the downstream repair proposal and its provenance carry the honesty tag rather than laundering an inferred verdict into apparent fact.

nodes.definition: Quarantine the truly-unverifiable. Quarantine means the edge is neither asserted true nor deleted nor corrected — it is held, tagged UNKNOWN, and surfaced for expert review, exactly as kgraph quarantines unsourced edges. This protects the graph from both a fabricated confirmation and a mistaken deletion of a proposition the system simply cannot verify with its current corpus.

nodes.definition: Lower autonomy when calibration is untrusted or drifts. workflow.description: Return UNKNOWN below threshold, measure abstention, and trigger deep verification only on contested edges
workflow.gate: the layer abstains below threshold, measures the rate, and gates deep retrieval on confidence

workflow.description: Combine evidence-grounded verdict, LLM-as-judge reliability, and cross-sample agreement; disagreement escalates
workflow.gate: multiple independent signals are combined and disagreement triggers abstain/escalate

workflow.action: Correct relation type or propose a negation
workflow.description: Output retype/direction-fix for a true-but-mistyped edge, or a negated edge for a contradicted one
workflow.gate: a mistyped-but-true edge is retyped not deleted, a contradicted edge can become a negation, schema legality deferred to kgraph

workflow.action: Label honesty and quarantine the unverifiable
workflow.description: Label FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN and quarantine no-evidence propositions
workflow.gate: every verdict is labeled, no-evidence is UNKNOWN-quarantined, and raw confidence is ESTIMATE

workflow.action: Map the verdict onto ConceptEdge and walk D2
workflow.description: Bind the verdict to ConceptEdge fields with an honesty tag and walk the malignancy example end-to-end
workflow.gate: the verdict maps to ConceptEdge with an honesty tag and D2 is processed verify-ground-retype-escalate-label

workflow.action: Commit the verification verdict and defer downstream
workflow.description: Commit the evidence-grounded, calibrated, abstaining verifier and the kgraph/viz/learner/kb3 deferrals
workflow.gate: the committed verifier emits typed honesty-tagged verdicts with confidence and defers repair to kb3 and structure to kgraph

priority_rationale: The committed verifier, evidence-grounding, and the D2 both-can-be-wrong lesson lead because they are the core that makes content verification honest and is the reason the specialist exists; verifying the human flag, calibrated confidence, abstention, the retype verdict, the overconfidence guard, honesty labeling and the D2 worked example form the operating discipline that turns a truth judgment into a safe, auditable, escalate-not-delete verdict; and the NLI primitive, the scope fence, the ConceptEdge mapping, UNKNOWN quarantine, multi-signal scoring, drift-lowers-autonomy, the negation verdict, the confidence gate, thin-node re-linking and the problem frame complete the layer, ordered later because they elaborate or ground the core rather than deciding truth.

dominance_rules.rule: Retrieved evidence dominates model memory for any clinical verdict
dominance_rules.rationale: kgverify must never assert clinical truth without a citation
dominance_rules.trigger: a verdict is about to rest on model memory
dominance_rules.action: require the verdict to trace to a retrieved chunk or return UNKNOWN

dominance_rules.rule: Verifying the flag dominates trusting the flag
dominance_rules.rationale: the owner's non-sequitur label can be wrong, as D2's real associations show
dominance_rules.trigger: an owner-flagged edge is about to be deleted
dominance_rules.action: verify against evidence and escalate a conflict to the owner; never delete on the flag alone

dominance_rules.rationale: a confidently-wrong proposal is worse than an abstention
dominance_rules.trigger: confidence is below the abstention threshold
dominance_rules.action: return UNKNOWN, quarantine, and route to human review

dominance_rules.rule: Calibrated, cross-checked confidence dominates raw model confidence
dominance_rules.rationale: LLMs are Dunning-Kruger overconfident in fact-checking
dominance_rules.trigger: a high stated confidence is about to gate action
dominance_rules.action: require evidence and cross-signal agreement, treat raw confidence as ESTIMATE, and lower autonomy on drift

dominance_rules.rule: Retype dominates delete for a true-but-mistyped edge
dominance_rules.rationale: deleting a real association because its edge is mistyped loses true information
dominance_rules.trigger: a flagged edge is plausibly true but wrongly typed
dominance_rules.action: propose a retype/direction-fix and hand the schema legality to kgraph

dominance_rules.rule: Negation dominates bare delete when the truth is a negation
dominance_rules.rationale: a delete erases a studyable non-relationship a negated edge preserves
dominance_rules.action: propose a negated edge rather than a bare delete and never render it positive

dominance_rules.rule: A required citation dominates re-linking a thin node
dominance_rules.rationale: inventing an uncited edge corrupts the graph with false authority
dominance_rules.action: propose only cited edges carried as ESTIMATE until human-confirmed

dominance_rules.rule: kb3 owner-gating and kgraph schema ownership dominate kgverify's verdict for any live change
dominance_rules.rationale: kgverify owns truth, not the write, the schema, the render or the schedule
dominance_rules.trigger: a verdict would change the live graph
dominance_rules.action: hand the verdict to kb3 for owner-gated write and to kgraph for schema legality; render to viz, schedule to learner/sched

anti_rework_rules.rule: Ground every verdict in retrieved evidence from the first pass
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a graph of confidently-labeled but memory-based verdicts that must later be re-verified

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the human flag before any delete
anti_rework_rules.prevents: deleting clinically real but surprising edges that must later be reconstructed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat raw model confidence as ESTIMATE and track ECE up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: acting on overconfident numbers and reworking every verdict when calibration is questioned

anti_rework_rules.rule: Make abstention and UNKNOWN-quarantine first-class outputs from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: forced verdicts on underdetermined propositions that must later be walked back

anti_rework_rules.rule: Prefer retype/negation over delete when truth allows
anti_rework_rules.prevents: deleting true-but-mistyped or contradicted-but-studyable edges and re-adding them later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the honesty tag at the verdict, not at the repair
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an inferred verdict being laundered into apparent fact downstream in kb3

anti_rework_rules.rule: Defer the write, schema, render and scheduling to their owners from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: kgverify silently rewriting edges and colliding with kgraph/viz/learner-sched

anti_rework_rules.rule: Require citations for thin-node re-links from the first proposal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an uncited-edge cleanup after the graph is thickened by fabrication

iteration_protocol.trigger: the verifier model or its calibration (ECE) is measured or changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-check calibration, adjust the abstention threshold, and re-label all confidences as ESTIMATE

iteration_protocol.trigger: an owner resolves a flag-vs-evidence escalation
iteration_protocol.action: record the resolution as the authoritative verdict and update the flagged edge's honesty tag

iteration_protocol.trigger: a retrieved citation confirms or refutes a CLINICAL-UNKNOWN association
iteration_protocol.action: promote the verdict from ESTIMATE toward FACT or to a negation/UNKNOWN accordingly

iteration_protocol.trigger: kgraph adds or refuses a relation type a retype needs
iteration_protocol.action: re-target the retype verdict onto the confirmed type or hold it pending the schema decision

iteration_protocol.trigger: the abstention rate or human-review queue swings out of band
iteration_protocol.action: re-tune the confidence threshold and the deep-path gate against selective-accuracy metrics

iteration_protocol.trigger: a real negated edge appears or viz ships the negation render contract
iteration_protocol.action: exercise the negation verdict on real data and align with the render contract

iteration_protocol.trigger: the retrieval corpus expands to cover previously-quarantined edges
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify UNKNOWN-quarantined propositions against the new evidence

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-22 nodes, 38-44 edges, 8-9 conflict_axes, 11-12 edge_cases, 10-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run
